newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom to double 97 payout - magazine.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom to double 97 payout - magazine.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG, slated for Germany's largest ever privatisation in November, plans to double its dividend payout in 1997 to a total three billion marks, news magazine Focus said on Saturday.
Focus sourced its report, released in advance of its Monday edition, to senior board members. A Telekom spokesman declined to comment.
Telekom finance director Joachim Koske recently said the 1996 dividend would be 1.5 billion marks and the shareholder payout next year would rank alongside other leading companies.
Focus said that the dividend, combined with tax breaks for investors, would mean that the Telekom shares would have a probable yield of six percent.

Telekom said on Friday it would publish a preliminary issue prospectus -- a so-called "Pink Herring" -- on October 4. But the number of shares to be offered by way of a capital increase and the flotation price will only be fixed later.
A range will be set when the "Red Herring" final prospectus is published on October 22, with the final share price to be fixed at the weekend ahead of the first listing on November 18.
